audience: Beginners who find studio culture intimidating, and regular practitioners looking for a second studio near work

services.name: Vinyasa
services.description: Flowing sequences set to breath, at a steady pace. 60 minutes, £14 drop-in.

services.name: Hatha
services.description: Slower held postures with detailed alignment. 75 minutes, £14 drop-in.

services.name: Yin
services.description: Long floor-based holds with bolsters and blocks provided. 60 minutes, £14 drop-in.

services.name: Beginners' course
services.description: A six-week course covering the postures that appear in every other class. £75 for the course.

services.name: Pregnancy yoga
services.description: For the second and third trimesters, taught by an instructor with a pregnancy-specific qualification. 60 minutes, £16 drop-in.

services.name: Mobility and strength
services.description: Loaded stretching and joint work, closer to a gym class than a yoga class. 45 minutes, £14 drop-in.

services.name: Sunrise practice
services.description: A short unheated class at 6.45am on weekdays. 45 minutes, £10 drop-in.

services.name: Studio hire
services.description: The larger room hires out for workshops and rehearsals at £30 an hour outside class times.

differentiators: Every class is capped at fourteen mats, so teachers can adjust individually
Mats, blocks, bolsters and straps are provided and included in the price
No membership and no contract — classes are booked one at a time or as a ten-class pass
Two studios in one building, so a beginners' class is never sharing a room with an advanced one
tone: Unpretentious and welcoming. No sanskrit without a translation, no talk of journeys or energy.
goals: Get first-time visitors to book the beginners' course rather than dropping into a general class
Sell ten-class passes to people who already practise
Fill the 6.45am slot, which is the emptiest on the timetable
